{'can_signal_faster_than_light': False, 'can_transmit_information': False, 'chsh_classical_max': 2.0, 'chsh_quantum_max': 2.8284271247461903, 'monogamy': 'If A is maximally entangled with B it cannot also be entangled with C — which is why an eavesdropper is detectable.', 'no_communication_theorem': "Local measurement outcomes are random and the marginal statistics on one side are independent of the partner's measurement choice — so entanglement alone transmits zero bits.", 'primary': False, 'requires_classical_channel': 'To USE the correlation (teleportation, key agreement) a separate classical channel at ≤ c is mandatory.', 'shared_resource': 'shared secret randomness: a private correlated key, the basis of quantum key distribution (Ekert E91).', 'verdict': 'NO — entangled particles cannot communicate or send information, faster than light or otherwise (the no-communication theorem). They share private correlated randomness, not a signal; extracting any message requires a separate classical channel at ≤ c.'} Entanglement is a correlation resource, not a communication channel. Faster-than-light signaling via entanglement is impossible; the only transferable thing is shared secret randomness, and using it needs a classical channel at ≤ c.
